text:
maria_g: Heads-up — ran a longctx batch job overnight (32k tokens, mixed seq lengths) and saw KV cache memory keep growing on H100 until OOM. Not classic leak, looks like eviction oscillation.
aj: Can you paste the eviction/alloc counters and a short timeline? :eyes:
maria_g: Sure, pasted below. The interesting bit is evict_rate spikes align with heavy small-batch bursts.
perf-bot: [auto] KV_EVICT_RATE=0.47 -> 0.92 (10m window), REUSE_HIT=0.12 -> 0.05, FRAG_SCORE=0.68 -> 0.81
maria_g: Timeline (rough):
- 00:00 warmup steady
- 00:12 spike in small seq requests (20-50 tokens)
- 00:12:30 eviction rate spikes, free pages increase then drop
- 00:20 memory RSS climbs steadily even after evict rate returns to baseline
cheng: Interesting. Could be repeated allocate->evict->realloc of same pages because of page table fragmentation. Any pagewalk stall logs?
maria_g: Got a snippet from the pager tracing:
```
PAGER: alloc page 0x3f4a
PAGER: evict page 0x3f4a -> remote free
PAGER: alloc page 0x4b2c (new slab)
PAGER: map shadow 0x3f4a -> 0x4b2c
PAGEWALK: long latency 8.4ms ctx=kvcache
```
sasha: That map back to different slot smells like aliasing; reuse window too short so we thrash between few slots.
aj: What kernel selection + batching config did you use? Sometimes different matmul kernels/memory ops affect allocation alignment.
maria_g: Using runtime default for H100: kernel=auto, batch_policy=latency, kv_prefetch=true. I tried forcing tiled-kernel and saw eviction spikes reduce but memory still grows slowly.
perf-bot: Quick perf counters (sampled at 1s):
- NVLINK_THROUGHPUT: 11.2GB/s
- PCIe_THROUGHPUT: 2.8GB/s
- PAGE_FAULTS/sec: 412
- ALLOC_FAILS/sec: 3
- KVCACHE_REUSE_HIT: 0.06

maria_g: Hypothesis: when small batches dominate, continuous-batching shrinks effective reuse window; page-table entries get scattered, coalescing heuristics fail and we create shadow mappings instead of reusing slots.
cheng: Could be exacerbated by the eviction threshold being hard cutover. We discussed smoothing the threshold (hysteresis + EWMA) to avoid flip-flop.
aj: Do you have an experiment patch? Even a config tweak to try locally would be helpful.
maria_g: Yes — added two knobs: evict_threshold_low, evict_threshold_high and smoothing_alpha. Example config I ran:
```
kvcache:
  evict_threshold_high: 0.82
  evict_threshold_low: 0.68
  smoothing_alpha: 0.25
  reuse_min_window: 50
```
(smoothing_alpha is EWMA applied to current occupancy before comparing to thresholds)
sasha: Results? Did hysteresis stop oscillation?
maria_g: Partial. Evict spikes reduced (max 0.68 -> 0.75) and PAGE_FAULTS/sec down ~30% but memory growth rate only dropped ~2x, still nonzero across 3h run. Fragmentation score decreased to 0.62.
perf-bot: New counters after run:
- KV_EVICT_RATE peak 0.75
- PAGE_FAULTS/sec 285
- REUSE_HIT 0.14
- FRAG_SCORE 0.61

aj: That's promising. The reuse hit bump is good. But slow memory creep suggests some stale shadow mappings or soft-tombstones in page table.
cheng: Can you dump a small pt map sample? We want to see chained tombstones or non-contiguous free runs.
maria_g: Pulled a condensed page table snapshot (slot, state):
```
slot 1024: taken -> owner=ctxA
slot 1025: tombstone -> age=37
slot 1026: free
slot 1027: taken -> owner=ctxB
slot 1028: tombstone -> age=41
slot 1029: free
```
You can see alternate tombstones between frees causing small free runs, prevents coalescing.
sasha: That pattern will cause allocator to fragment and prefer new slabs, leading to memory growth. Need compaction or tombstone reclamation after N ops.
aj: Another angle: architecture differences. Do you see same on A100/MI250X?
maria_g: Ran quick sanity on A100 and MI250X. A100 shows similar behavior but slower pagewalk latency, MI250X had far fewer tombstones but worse eviction rate due to smaller vram-per-slab granularity.
cheng: So fix needs two parts: (1) allocation compaction/reuse heuristics to prefer reclaiming aged tombstones, (2) threshold smoothing to avoid churn, plus (3) small-batch batching policy change to maintain reuse window.
maria_g: Agreed. I sketched a reclaim pass that scans tombstone runs > X and coalesces into a free run and then signals the pager to remap. Also a batching tweak: when small-batch bursts detected, temporarily force batch_policy=throughput to enlarge reuse window.
ops-bot: Deploy plan comment: keep experimental flags behind runtime feature flag; roll canary 10% of H100 fleet for 12h, monitor PAGE_FAULTS and KV_EVICT_RATE.
aj: Let's add a telemetry gauge for tombstone density and a regression alert if memoryRSS growth > 1%/hr over 3h.
maria_g: I'll open a PR with the reclaim pass + config flags and add perf metrics. Will also run the canary on H100/A100/MI to compare.
cheng: Thanks — if you can attach the raw pager trace and pt dumps in the PR that'd speed review. Also include the small reproducer script if possible.
maria_g: Will do. For context: reproducer is a synthetic longctx generator with interleaved small-batch bursts. Simple python gist: https://gists.internal/repro/kv-paged-smallburst
sasha: Nice. If the reclaim pass works we should see FRAG_SCORE drop under 0.45 and reuse_hit > 0.2 in 30m runs.
perf-bot: [auto] scheduled canary monitor job pending
maria_g: Thanks all. Filing issue with logs and timeline. Ping me if you want to pair on the reclaim pass tomorrow. :thumbsup:
